newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht eases late on high weekend dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht eases late on high weekend dlr demand.

text.p: The Thai baht fell sharply in late Friday trade on strong demand for the U.S. dollar ahead of a long weekend, dealers said.
"The coming long weekend prompted people to adjust their positions. Players short on dollar actively bid for the greenback today," said one dealer at a local bank.
The baht was quoted at 30.42/30.47 per dollar late in the onshore market compared with 30.12/30.22 in the morning.
Monday is a public holiday to commemorate the start of Buddhist Lent.
Dealers said exporters delayed selling dollar positions in anticipation of further baht weakness.
"With the thin market, small transactions can easily move the (baht/dollar) rate," the dealer said.

The offshore baht was traded at 30.35/30.45 late against 30.08/30.18 in the early morning. The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was quoted at 27/34 satangs per dollar late in the domestic market and 65/85 satangs offhsore.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 14-15 percent late from 17-18 in the morning on higher liquidity, dealers said.
